titles: Russia Built Cities Where No Economy Should Exist
Why Is Russia So Big but So Empty? Follow the Money
The World Bank Paid Russians to Leave the Far North. Most Stayed
thumbnails: 1: NASA Black Marble, Russia at night (bright west, dark east), one lone light circled: "WHY HERE?"
2: Norilsk from Landsat (NASA, PD): "NO ROADS IN"
3: Prokudin-Gorsky colour photo of the Trans-Siberian bridge (LoC, PD): "PAID TO STAY"
hook: Russia has more large cities in cold places than any other country (Fiona Hill, Brookings). Why build cities where no market ever would, what does the cold cost every winter, and why did most people stay when the World Bank helped pay them to leave? The Siberian curse, explained with maps, charts and real numbers. No background needed. Not financial advice.

pinned_comment: Hill and Gaddy say Russia's real problem is not its size but where its people live. Would you move to Norilsk for double pay? Yes or no, and why?
